title: Add per-invocation cost estimator and trace-affinity metrics
author: Priya Nambiar
ci_status: pass (one flaky unit test retried and resolved)
release_notes: Adds a lightweight per-invocation cost estimator and trace-affinity metrics; new dashboard panels for per-invocation cost distribution and predicted token burn; introduces heuristic alert suppression window and cache-warm signal for long-tail alerts; no runtime breaking changes.
description: Context: Our long-tail latency and billing alerts frequently surface noisy cases where downstream token expansion or early-exit behavior inflates apparent cost. This PR introduces a cheap per-invocation cost estimator that runs at the edge of the serving runtime and a 'trace-affinity' propagation tag that helps link downstream async work back to the originating invocation. Goals: 1) provide a low-cost early signal for true invocation cost before full token accounting arrives, 2) reduce alert noise by exposing a cache-warm / estimated-cost signal for short suppression windows, 3) enable dashboards that let SREs and platform owners quickly triage whether an incident is billing-related or structural. What I changed: Implemented a probabilistic estimator (edge probe) that samples a small prefix and predicts final token burn using a light-weight ridge regressor trained on historical invocation features; added trace-affinity middleware to propagate an invocation affinity tag across async workers and external retriable requests; exported three new Prometheus metrics: redwood_invocation_estimated_tokens_total, redwood_invocation_estimate_confidence, redwood_trace_affinity_coupled_spans_total; added two panels to the Console dashboard: Invocation Cost Distribution (estimated vs actual) and Affinity Link Rate; tuned alert rules to include an estimated_cost window and a transient suppression flag when cache-warm signal is asserted; added unit and integration tests and documentation. Commits summary: - feat(telemetry): add invocation cost estimator and probe - feat(tracing): propagate trace-affinity tag across go/rust workers - perf: expose estimator confidence and histogram bucketing - docs: add observability guide and dashboard JSON - test: add deterministic test harness and flaky-case regression fix Changed areas (high level): inference/telemetry/invocation_cost_estimator.py; runtime/tracing/affinity_middleware.go; pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go; console/dashboards/invocation_cost.json; docs/observability/invocation_cost.md; tests/test_invocation_cost.py; ci/workflows/observability.yml; scripts/bench/estimate_probes.py; infra/helm/values-observability.yaml. Testing and CI: One unit test intermittently failed under race conditions against the estimator RNG on the first run; I added deterministic seeding and retried the CI job. Final CI status: all checks passing, coverage for the telemetry package unchanged within tolerance. Review conversation (summary): Marcus asked for cost estimator explainability and requested adding a 95th percentile confidence bucket; author responded and added the confidence metric and a small doc section describing model features. Sofia requested a minimal runtime overhead audit; I added microbenchmarks (scripts/bench) and included numbers in the PR description. Daniel asked to gate the affinity tag behind a runtime flag for Private deployments; implemented and added helm value values.observability.enableTraceAffinity=false as default. Approvals: Marcus approved after changes; Sofia approved pending a small doc tweak which was added; Daniel approved. Merge: Squash merge into main with conventional commit message and changelog entry. Rollout plan: Feature gated by helm flag and runtime feature flag; enable in canary for 24h, monitor redwood_invocation_estimate_confidence and affinity link rate. Observability follow-ups: Add an aggregation job to compute estimator drift weekly and wire an alert when mean absolute error > 10% over a week (ENG-2031). Related work: ties to ENG-1879 (long-tail alert reduction) and complements existing token attribution work but differs by providing an early, low-cost signal for routing suppression and triage.
